## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet. The starting architecture scored 0.000 dev success on both seeds, so I can't tell yet whether the problem is learning or generalisation. Following the program's round-1 split, the three candidates are:
(a) Recipe only: ppo_epochs drops from 4 to 2, giving about 243k steps. gamma rises to 0.98 and gae_lambda to 0.95 so the +1 exact-build bonus counts back further across episodes of 6–33 steps. Rollouts are longer.
(b) Architecture only, with the default recipe: a deeper, narrower residual 2D network where each block gets global context from pooled features, plus near-zero initial output weights so the starting policy is close to uniform. Compute is about 1.2× the start.
(c) Both changes together.
Exact builds are rare, so while dev success stays at 0 I will rank candidates by mean training success and the training signals.

### Round 2
All three round-1 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success, so this is a learning problem, not a generalisation problem. Neither the recipe change (2 epochs, about 1.75× the steps, longer horizon) nor the deeper residual network with global context helped. Runs take only about 65 s, so time is not the limit. With FLOPs ratio r ≤ 1, the only way to get more samples is fewer epochs: ppo_epochs=1 gives about 426k steps. The likely bottleneck is perceiving where a brick will land. An exact placement needs the landing layer, which is the maximum build height under the footprint, and then the target at that layer for every footprint cell. The 2D trunk with height as channels has to learn that comparison indirectly. This round tests a layer-factored network: a learned MLP shared across layers, pooling over each footprint on every layer, and learned attention over layers to pick the landing layer. Its compute is about the start's. It runs with two recipes, plus a recipe-only control on the starting network.

### Round 3
All six trials scored 0 on dev and 0 on training success in the last 10% of training. That held for 1, 2 and 4 epochs, 102k to 426k steps, gamma 0.95 to 0.98, and three different conv networks. The reports give no other training signal, so the trials cannot be ranked, and none of the changes moved anything. Recipe tweaks alone look exhausted. Every network so far shared one assumption: per-cell logits from translation-equivariant convolutions, mapped to actions by the described index layout. If this world's action layout or grid orientation differs from the description, that kind of head cannot express a correct policy at all, which would fit training success staying at exactly 0 everywhere. This round tests that directly. Candidate 1 adds a flat learned action head alongside the conv head. Candidate 2 is a pure MLP that assumes no layout. Candidate 3 is a conv trunk with only a flat head. All three also feed the mask in as an input. If none of them learns, the next suspects are collapse onto DONE or a sparse reward.

### Round 4
All 9 trials ended with 0 dev success and 0 training success on both seeds. That covers 1–2 epochs, 100k–426k steps, gamma 0.95–0.98, conv heads, a layer-factored head, flat linear heads and a pure MLP. The failure is in learning, not generalisation. More samples, a longer horizon, footprint pooling and a layout-free flat head each failed to move training success off zero. The flat and MLP heads may simply learn too slowly to test whether the action layout is wrong. Three things are untested: the legality mask as an input feature; a cheap, translation-equivariant head that still copes with a transposed or flipped action layout; and a low-entropy, higher-lr recipe that lets the policy commit sharply. Exact builds need about 10 correct steps in a row, so a diffuse policy almost never succeeds. This is the last round. If nothing beats 0, the starting network is selected anyway, so these candidates are deliberately varied bets.
